text:
emma_support: Hey team — ACME Media (tenant_id=acme_media_77) reporting repeated 429s and spike in tail latency on Dedicated pool eu-west-1-ded-42 since 2025-11-02T11:52:10Z. Sample req id req_0a3f2b. Response body: {"error":"rate_limit","code":429,"message":"quota exceeded"}
rahul_eng: Thanks — can you paste the tenant plan and the last billing/quota change? Also any repro curl? :mag:
emma_support: Plan is "team-reserved-1"; last plan change was 2025-10-28 (no manual quota edits). Customer provided repro:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/respond \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme_media_77" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-4x-redwood","input":"short prompt"}'
```
Response header excerpt: `x-rl-remaining: 0`, `x-rl-reset: 3600`
josh_prod: Quick glance at alerting — tenant-alert-bot fired a sustained 429 alert at 11:52:15, rate of 429s ~120/min. No pool-wide capacity alerts. Could be per-tenant throttle.
lina_sre: I'm seeing config migration job ran 2025-10-30 to normalize quota units. There's a suspicious delta: DB shows per_tenant.quota_units=600 and per_tenant.quota_period='minute' but rate-service interprets period in seconds due to a bug. That makes effective quota 600/sec -> actually much higher not lower, hmm. Need to check migration diff.
rahul_eng: Repro on staging: I tried applying the same JSON config and the enforcement layer expects "rate_unit" to be "minute|hour|second" and our new migration column stores plural like "minutes". That mismatch caused fallback to default small quota (100 units/min) for some tenants. Possible root cause: migration script trimmed s->singular inconsistently.
emma_support: So some tenants got fallback quotas, explains sudden 429s while pool capacity unused. Customer says they didn't change anything.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rate-service v2.11 deployed 2025-10-30 02:13 UTC (canary succeeded). No rollbacks.
rahul_eng: Actionables: 1) SRE to run query to list tenants where quota_period not in [second,minute,hour]. 2) Support to request temporary quota-override for acme_media_77. 3) Hotfix migration to normalize historical values, and new validation in rate-service.
lina_sre: Run this query to enumerate affected tenants:
```
SELECT tenant_id, quota_units, quota_period FROM per_tenant WHERE quota_period NOT IN ('second','minute','hour');
```
I already found ~18 tenants with quota_period like 'minutes' or 'mins'.
maria_billing: For ACME I can push a temporary override until SRE fixes it. What number should we set?
rahul_eng: Set temporary override to 6000/min (equivalent to what they were expecting) and add note to expire in 48h. Also attach audit id to the change.
emma_support: Done — created override ticket SUP-3321, applied override, customer reports 429s dropped to zero within 2m and latency normalized. :relieved:
lina_sre: Confirmed — after override, x-rl-remaining present and >0. Patching migration now: will add normalization step to map plural forms to singular, and add schema constraint so invalid values are rejected at write. Plan to roll patch in next 2 hours with canary.
josh_prod: Suggest follow-ups: 1) run bulk normalization backfill for historical tenants 2) add a dashboard showing quota fallback events (when service sets default small quota) 3) postmortem with timeline and customer impact.
rahul_eng: I will open GH PR for migration hotfix and a unit test for plural edge-case. Lina, can you coordinate the canary and rollback plan?
lina_sre: Yep. Canary to 5% traffic, monitor 429 rate, deploy-bot will annotate.
rahul_eng: Also added a quick mitig in rate-service: if tenant's quota appears to be the fallback default and a recent plan-change was detected -> treat as suspect and auto-surface to ops dashboard.
emma_support: Customer happy for now but asked for root-cause note and ETA for permanent fix. Sharing this thread with them.
ops-bot: incident-bot created incident INC-20251102-7 for tracking (severity: high, owner: eng-rate).
josh_prod: Thanks team. Emma, please update SUP-3321 with incident link and customer-facing summary. We'll follow up with postmortem within 48 hours. :white_check_mark:
